summary:
CoastPulse is an advanced Earth Observation platform engineered to address the critical vulnerability of coastal deltas and wetlands to sea-level rise, cyclone surges, and erosion. details:
What CoastPulse Does & How It Works

CoastPulse is a multi-sensor coastal resilience and satellite observation platform that monitors fragile coastal deltas, tidal wetlands, and shorelines. Traditional optical imagery is frequently blinded by clouds and precipitation during storms—precisely when disaster intelligence is needed most. CoastPulse solves this by processing cloud-penetrating Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) from NASA-ISRO NISAR (L-band) and Copernicus Sentinel-1 (C-band).

The architecture operates in three synchronized stages:

  1. Scientific Ingestion & Processing: High-performance Python pipelines calibrate raw radar swaths into terrain-flattened, Float32 gamma-nought (dB) co-polarized (HH) and cross-polarized (HV) backscatter rasters.
  2. Automated Algorithmic Derivation: The engine runs dynamic Otsu adaptive thresholding for flood inundation mapping, calculates the Muthupet mangrove Radar Vegetation Index (RVI), and computes 12-day repeat orbit log-ratio change detection.
  3. Reactive 3D WebGL Visualization: A Next.js frontend renders all 15 geospatial layers with custom color ramps, allowing users to switch seamlessly into a 60-degree oblique 3D perspective, simulate storm surges, and analyze shoreline transects.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • All-Weather Situational Awareness: Provides 24/7 disaster monitoring regardless of weather, darkness, or monsoonal cloud cover.
  • Proactive Coastal Protection: Allows environmental managers and civil protection agencies to identify erosion hotspots (such as active dune retreat at -3.1 meters/year) before catastrophic breaches occur.
  • Scientific Integrity & Reproducibility: Every observation includes cryptographic SHA-256 provenance hashes and ISO 19115 compliant metadata, ensuring zero fabricated data.
  • Direct GIS Interoperability: Coastal planners can export calibrated layers directly to GeoJSON, Georeferenced Rasters, and tabular CSV statistics for QGIS/ArcGIS workflows.

Tools, Languages, & Software Architecture

  • Frontend: Next.js 16 (React 19), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL (custom WebGL shaders), Lucide Icons, and Recharts.
  • Scientific Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, SciPy (Otsu & speckle filtering), GeoPandas, and Rasterio/GDAL.
  • Database & Persistence: SQLite with SQLAlchemy ORM and aiosqlite for asynchronous queries (under 2ms latency).
  • Marine Telemetry & Ocean Models: Integrated Open-Meteo Marine API, NOAA harmonic tide predictions, and the empirical Stockdon (2006) parametric wave runup (R2%) equations.

Creative Innovations & Key Design Factors

  • Interactive 3D Oblique Perspectives: Unlike static 2D web maps, a single click tilts the view to 60 degrees, giving emergency planners natural depth perception over coastal terrain.
  • Animated Storm Surge Simulator: Allows users to slide and animate Total Water Level (TWL) surges from +0.5 meters to +3.0 meters, dynamically calculating submerged acreage in real time.
  • Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS): Interactive transect tools plot 2D coastal elevation profiles from inland berms to nearshore zones, reporting historic displacement rates.
  • Edge & Offline Readiness: Designed with lightweight tile serving and sub-10ms in-memory grid caching, enabling responsive operation even over constrained field networks.
